planting_dates_description.transplant: Not Recommended
planting_dates_description.start_outdoors: Directly sow arugula seeds outdoors in spring in April to May as soon as soil can be worked.
planting_dates_description.harvest: Harvest arugula leaves in late spring to early summer in May to June. Plant will bolt as temperatures warm.

planting_dates_description.start_indoors: Not Recommended
planting_dates_description.transplant: Not Recommended
planting_dates_description.start_outdoors: Directly sow arugula seeds outdoors in early spring in March to April and again in late summer in August to September for fall harvest.
planting_dates_description.harvest: Harvest in spring and again in fall. Arugula is ideal for spring and fall gardens when temperatures are cool.

planting_dates_description.start_indoors: Not Recommended
planting_dates_description.transplant: Not Recommended
planting_dates_description.start_outdoors: Directly sow arugula seeds outdoors in early spring in February to March and in late summer in August to September.
planting_dates_description.harvest: Harvest in spring and fall. Summer plantings will bolt quickly, so focus on cool season growing.

planting_dates_description.start_indoors: Not Recommended
planting_dates_description.transplant: Not Recommended
planting_dates_description.start_outdoors: Directly sow arugula seeds outdoors in fall and winter in October to January.
planting_dates_description.harvest: Harvest from late fall through winter. Arugula thrives in cool season conditions in these zones.

planting_dates_description.start_indoors: Not Recommended
planting_dates_description.transplant: Not Recommended
planting_dates_description.start_outdoors: Directly sow arugula seeds outdoors in winter months when temperatures cool.
planting_dates_description.harvest: Harvest during cool season months in winter.

varieties.name: Roquette (Wild Arugula)
varieties.description: Roquette, or wild arugula, is a smaller-leafed, deeply lobed variety with a more intense, peppery flavor than cultivated arugula. This heirloom Italian variety produces tender, delicate leaves perfect for salads and Italian cuisine. It grows quickly and is highly cold tolerant, making it ideal for cool season gardens.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, keep soil consistently moist
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light to moderate fertility, optional light fertilizer

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Very peppery, intense, spicy with sharp mustard-like notes

leafCropCharacteristics.bolt_resistance: Moderate, will bolt in warm weather

varieties.fun_fact: Wild arugula (Diplotaxis tenuifolia) is a different species from cultivated arugula and actually has a more peppery bite. In Italy, it's considered more sophisticated and is often paired with aged cheeses and truffle oil.
varieties.planting_tip: Roquette is best grown in cool seasons and prefers partial shade in warmer weather to slow bolting. Direct sow seeds in early spring or late summer for best results. Space plants 4-6 inches apart for tender leaves or closer for micro greens. Harvest outer leaves when they reach 2-3 inches for continuous picking, or wait 30-40 days for full plant maturity. This variety thrives in containers and is ideal for quick succession plantings every 2-3 weeks for continuous harvest.

varieties.name: Astro
varieties.description: Astro is a modern hybrid arugula variety bred for slow bolting and extended harvest periods. This cultivar produces broad, tender leaves with a classic peppery arugula flavor that's slightly milder than wild arugula. It's excellent for commercial production and home gardeners seeking reliability and longer harvest windows.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, consistent moisture preferred
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light to moderate fertility

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Peppery, balanced, slightly milder than wild arugula with pleasant nutty undertones

leafCropCharacteristics.bolt_resistance: Very good, slower to bolt than other varieties

varieties.fun_fact: Astro arugula was specifically developed to solve the common problem of arugula bolting too quickly in home gardens, giving home gardeners a longer window for harvest.
varieties.planting_tip: Astro is more forgiving than traditional arugula and can handle slightly warmer temperatures before bolting. Direct sow seeds in early spring or mid to late summer for fall harvest. Keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged. Thin seedlings to 4-6 inches for full-sized plants or leave closer together for tender baby leaves. Begin harvesting outer leaves when they're 2-3 inches long for continuous picking. This variety works particularly well for succession planting every 2 weeks for continuous supply.

varieties.name: Arugula Sylvetta
varieties.description: Arugula Sylvetta is a cultivated variety of wild arugula that offers a good balance between the intense flavor of true wild arugula and the ease of growing cultivated varieties. It produces deeply lobed leaves with a distinctly peppery flavor and better cold tolerance than standard arugula. This variety is increasingly popular in specialty salad mixes.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, keep soil moist
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light fertility, minimal fertilizer needed

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Intensely peppery with complex spicy notes, more flavorful than standard arugula

varieties.fun_fact: Sylvetta arugula is sometimes called 'Japanese arugula' in specialty seed catalogs, though it has no connection to Japan—the name likely refers to its sophisticated flavor profile.
varieties.planting_tip: Sylvetta arugula prefers cool growing conditions and thrives in spring and fall gardens. Direct sow seeds 1/4 inch deep in well-prepared, moist soil. Space plants 4-6 inches apart for full-sized plants. This variety is excellent for succession planting and provides several harvests before bolting. Pick outer leaves regularly starting when they're 2-3 inches long to extend the harvest period. For best flavor and tenderness, harvest in cool morning hours. Excellent for container gardening and grows well as microgreens.

varieties.name: Runway
varieties.description: Runway is a heat-tolerant arugula variety bred specifically for extended growing seasons and resistance to bolting. This modern hybrid produces large, tender leaves with a mild, pleasant peppery flavor. It's ideal for summer gardens and warm climates where traditional arugula struggles, making it a game-changer for year-round arugula lovers.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, consistent moisture especially in warm weather
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Moderate fertility, benefits from balanced fertilizer

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Mild to moderate peppery flavor, less bitter than standard arugula with pleasant nutty notes

leafCropCharacteristics.leaf_texture: Large, broad, smooth with slight serration

varieties.fun_fact: Runway arugula can extend the arugula growing season by 4-6 weeks compared to traditional varieties, making it possible to grow arugula through most of summer in many climates!
varieties.planting_tip: Runway's heat tolerance makes it ideal for succession planting from spring through early fall. Direct sow seeds every 2-3 weeks for continuous harvest. While heat-tolerant, it still benefits from afternoon shade in extreme heat (above 85°F). Keep soil consistently moist during warm weather to maintain leaf tenderness and reduce bitterness. Harvest outer leaves when 3-4 inches long for best flavor. This variety is perfect for gardeners who've struggled with arugula bolting in their climate.

varieties.name: Dragon's Tongue
varieties.description: Dragon's Tongue is a distinctive arugula variety featuring deeply serrated, purple-tinged leaves that add visual drama to salads. This heirloom-type variety offers an exceptionally spicy, mustard-like flavor that intensifies as leaves mature. The burgundy veining becomes more pronounced in cool weather, making it both a culinary and ornamental choice for specialty gardens.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, consistent moisture for best color development
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light to moderate fertility

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Very spicy, intense peppery-mustard flavor with sharp, assertive bite

leafCropCharacteristics.leaf_texture: Deeply serrated, tender with prominent veining

varieties.fun_fact: Dragon's Tongue arugula's purple coloration intensifies with cold exposure, making fall-grown leaves the most visually striking—and the most flavorful! The color comes from anthocyanins, powerful antioxidants.
varieties.planting_tip: Dragon's Tongue thrives in cool weather and develops its best color and flavor after light frosts. Direct sow in early spring or late summer for fall harvest. Space plants slightly wider (6-8 inches) to showcase the beautiful leaf patterns. Harvest young leaves for milder flavor or wait for mature leaves for maximum spice and color. The distinctive appearance makes this variety popular for farmers markets and gourmet restaurants. Grows exceptionally well in containers where the colorful foliage can be displayed.

varieties.name: Wasabi
varieties.description: Wasabi arugula is a specialty variety with an exceptionally sharp, wasabi-like heat that sets it apart from traditional arugula. This fast-growing variety produces bright green, lobed leaves with an intense, spicy kick perfect for those who love bold flavors. It's becoming increasingly popular in Asian fusion cuisine and among adventurous gardeners seeking unique flavors.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, keep soil consistently moist for best flavor
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light fertility, minimal fertilizer needed

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Extremely spicy with sharp, wasabi-like heat and intense peppery notes

leafCropCharacteristics.bolt_resistance: Low, bolts quickly in warm weather

varieties.fun_fact: Wasabi arugula doesn't actually contain wasabi compounds, but its intense spiciness comes from similar glucosinolates that create a nose-tingling heat reminiscent of real wasabi!
varieties.planting_tip: Wasabi arugula is extremely fast-growing and best harvested young for peak spiciness. Direct sow seeds in cool weather (spring or fall) and keep soil consistently moist—dry conditions make the leaves even more intensely spicy and tough. Harvest leaves when they're 1-2 inches long for the perfect balance of tenderness and heat. This variety is excellent for microgreens and baby leaf production. Space closely (3-4 inches) for tender baby leaves. The intense flavor means a little goes a long way in dishes!

varieties.name: Bellezia
varieties.description: Bellezia is a premium Italian arugula variety known for its tender texture and refined, balanced flavor. This cultivated variety produces uniform, rounded leaves with smooth edges and a sophisticated peppery taste that's milder than wild arugula but more flavorful than standard varieties. It's a favorite among chefs for its consistent quality and elegant appearance.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, consistent moisture for tender leaves
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Moderate fertility, benefits from rich soil

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Balanced peppery flavor with sweet undertones, refined and sophisticated

leafCropCharacteristics.bolt_resistance: Good, slower to bolt than heirlooms

varieties.fun_fact: Bellezia arugula is grown extensively in the Veneto region of Italy and is the preferred variety for traditional Venetian salads where its tender texture and refined flavor shine!
varieties.planting_tip: Bellezia performs best in enriched soil with good moisture retention. Direct sow seeds in early spring or late summer, spacing 5-6 inches apart for full-sized leaves. This variety benefits from light shade during the hottest part of the day to maintain tender texture. Harvest outer leaves when 2-4 inches long for continuous production. The refined flavor and attractive appearance make this variety excellent for market gardening and upscale restaurants. Grows beautifully in containers with consistent watering.

varieties.name: Red Dragon
varieties.description: Red Dragon is a striking arugula variety featuring deep burgundy-red leaves with an intense, spicy flavor. This ornamental and culinary variety produces oak-leaf shaped foliage with rich coloration that intensifies in cool weather. Red Dragon offers both visual appeal and robust flavor, making it a standout in gourmet salad mixes and specialty gardens.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, consistent moisture for color development
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light to moderate fertility, avoid excess nitrogen

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Intensely peppery and spicy with bold, assertive flavor and slight bitterness

varieties.fun_fact: Red Dragon arugula's dramatic coloring comes from extremely high anthocyanin levels—the same antioxidants found in blueberries and red wine! The deeper the color, the more antioxidants present.
varieties.planting_tip: Red Dragon develops its most intense color when grown in cool temperatures (below 65°F) with plenty of sunlight. Direct sow in early spring or late summer for fall harvest. Space plants 6-8 inches apart to showcase the beautiful foliage. The deep red color makes this variety stunning in containers and ornamental gardens. Harvest young leaves for tender texture and less bitterness. Cool night temperatures intensify the burgundy coloration. Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer, which can reduce color intensity and increase green growth.

varieties.name: Apollo
varieties.description: Apollo is a fast-growing, uniform arugula variety bred for commercial production and home gardens seeking reliability. This hybrid produces broad, dark green leaves with a well-balanced peppery flavor that appeals to a wide range of palates. Apollo has excellent disease resistance and consistent germination, making it a dependable choice for succession planting and year-round production.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, consistent moisture preferred
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Moderate fertility, benefits from balanced fertilizer

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Balanced peppery flavor, moderately spicy with pleasant nutty notes

leafCropCharacteristics.leaf_texture: Broad, smooth, tender with slight serration

varieties.fun_fact: Apollo arugula was bred specifically for its exceptional uniformity and germination rates—nearly 95% germination under ideal conditions makes it a favorite for market gardeners and commercial growers!
varieties.planting_tip: Apollo's reliable germination and fast growth make it perfect for succession planting every 10-14 days for continuous harvest. Direct sow seeds 1/4 inch deep in prepared soil with good drainage. Space 4-6 inches apart for full-sized leaves or closer for baby greens. This variety performs well in both spring and fall gardens and tolerates light shade in warmer weather. Begin harvesting outer leaves when 2-3 inches long. The uniform growth pattern makes Apollo ideal for one-cut baby leaf production.

varieties.name: Rustic
varieties.description: Rustic is a robust arugula variety that combines the deep flavor of wild arugula with the productivity of cultivated types. This variety produces deeply lobed, dark green leaves with an earthy, complex peppery flavor. Rustic is particularly cold-hardy and slow to bolt, making it ideal for fall and winter gardens in mild climates or cold frame production.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Moderate watering, tolerates some dryness once established
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Light fertility, minimal fertilizer needed

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Complex, earthy peppery flavor with pronounced spiciness and slight bitterness

leafCropCharacteristics.leaf_texture: Deeply lobed, sturdy, slightly thicker than standard arugula

varieties.fun_fact: Rustic arugula can survive temperatures down to 10°F with protection, making it one of the most cold-hardy salad greens available! In mild climates, it can be harvested throughout winter.
varieties.planting_tip: Rustic excels as a fall and winter crop in zones 7-10 or under cold frames/row covers in colder zones. Direct sow in late summer or early fall for winter harvest. Space plants 6-8 inches apart to accommodate the larger rosette size. The robust leaves hold up better in cold weather than tender varieties. This variety's slower growth means longer time to harvest but extended productive period. Excellent for overwintering in hoop houses or unheated greenhouses. Harvest outer leaves as needed throughout winter.

varieties.name: Olive Leaf
varieties.description: Olive Leaf is a unique arugula variety with distinctive narrow, elongated leaves resembling olive tree foliage. This specialty variety offers a mild, sophisticated peppery flavor with subtle herbal notes. The unusual leaf shape and refined taste make it popular in upscale restaurants and among gardeners seeking something different from standard arugula varieties.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, consistent moisture for tender leaves
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Moderate fertility

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Mild to moderate peppery flavor with subtle herbal, slightly grassy notes

varieties.fun_fact: Olive Leaf arugula's unusual narrow leaves are not only visually distinctive but also have a higher surface area to volume ratio, which creates a unique texture in the mouth compared to broad-leafed varieties!
varieties.planting_tip: Olive Leaf arugula grows best in cool spring and fall conditions. Direct sow seeds in well-prepared soil with good drainage. Space plants 5-7 inches apart to showcase the distinctive leaf shape. The unique appearance makes this variety excellent for visual interest in mixed salad greens. Harvest individual leaves when 3-4 inches long or cut entire plant 1 inch above soil for regrowth. The mild flavor makes it versatile for dishes where you want arugula's character without overwhelming spice. Popular with chefs for creative plating.

varieties.name: Slow Bolt
varieties.description: Slow Bolt is a heat-tolerant arugula variety specifically bred to resist bolting and extend the harvest season into warmer weather. This variety produces medium-sized, serrated leaves with a classic peppery arugula flavor that remains balanced even as temperatures rise. Slow Bolt is ideal for gardeners in warmer climates or those seeking longer production windows.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular to frequent watering, especially in warm weather
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Moderate fertility, consistent feeding for extended production

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Classic peppery arugula flavor, moderately spicy with pleasant balance

varieties.fun_fact: Slow Bolt arugula can continue producing for 4-6 weeks longer than standard varieties before flowering, potentially doubling the harvest window in optimal conditions!
varieties.planting_tip: Slow Bolt performs best with consistent moisture and benefits from afternoon shade in hot climates (above 80°F). Direct sow in spring and continue planting through early summer for extended harvest. Space 4-6 inches apart and mulch around plants to keep roots cool and conserve moisture. Even with its heat tolerance, harvesting regularly encourages continued leaf production and delays bolting. Begin harvesting when leaves reach 2-3 inches. This variety bridges the gap between spring and fall arugula crops in many climates.

varieties.name: Grazia
varieties.description: Grazia is a premium Italian arugula variety prized for its exceptionally tender texture and sweet-peppery flavor profile. This cultivated variety produces uniform, rounded leaves with minimal bitterness and a buttery texture. Grazia is a favorite among chefs for its delicate flavor that doesn't overpower other salad ingredients while still providing characteristic arugula taste.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, consistent moisture essential for tender texture
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Moderate fertility, benefits from rich, well-amended soil

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Delicately peppery with sweet undertones, minimal bitterness, buttery texture

leafCropCharacteristics.leaf_texture: Smooth, rounded, exceptionally tender and buttery

varieties.fun_fact: Grazia arugula is named after the Italian word for 'grace' or 'elegance,' reflecting its refined flavor and delicate texture that has made it a staple in high-end Italian restaurants!
varieties.planting_tip: Grazia requires rich, moisture-retentive soil and consistent watering to develop its signature tender texture. Direct sow seeds in early spring or late summer, spacing 5-6 inches apart. This variety benefits from light shade during the hottest part of the day to maintain tenderness and sweetness. Harvest young leaves at 2-3 inches for peak tenderness and sweetness. The delicate flavor makes it perfect for simple salads with light vinaigrettes where you want subtle peppery notes. Excellent for baby leaf production and mesclun mixes. Popular in containers with regular watering.
